### 2026-10-24 – Most of this was planned a couple days ago, but I've been really busy and haven't thought too post it yet. But here's my idea, I'm making a thermon. With 2 ultrasonic distance sensors connecting to a

**4h**

Most of this was planned a couple days ago, but I've been really busy and haven't thought too post it yet. But here's my idea, I'm making a thermon. With 2 ultrasonic distance sensors connecting to a arduino, Uno, as the brain and then off-putting those signals into sound signals, and then that exiting through a speaker, I've done a lot of brainstorming of different ideas that I could do. And then weighed the pros and cons in researched each idea and then researched a bunch into how theramans worked
 And finally, designed kind of a simple wiring plan for my theraman.

### 2026-10-24 – This session, I spent entirely coding, and seeing if it was actually possible to use the pieces that I wanted to use to make a theramine. Recently, I've been trying to only use the textbakes coding, i

**4h**

This session, I spent entirely coding, and seeing if it was actually possible to use the pieces that I wanted to use to make a theramine. Recently, I've been trying to only use the textbakes coding, instead of the block based coating on dingercad, which has made it a lot longer of a process than it was before, because I am a very beginner when it comes to coding. I spent a long time trying to make it. So one ultrasonic distance sensor would control the pitch and the other ultrasonic distance sensor would control the volume. But I found out that it's not actually possible to control the volume of a speaker in tinker cad, through digital means. This means the code that I made isn't really a final code. And i'm going to fix it once I have a physical product. But currently I have an ultrasonic sensor connected to an arduino uno that controls the pitch of a speaker. I also tried for a while connecting up a potentiometer to control the volume. But that didn't work either. I'm excited to continue working on this project to make it real.

This session I made the entirety of the schematic and the entirety of the repo. I started by making the schematic so that I could put it into the repo one problem there was, is there's no ultrasonic sensor connectors in kicad so I had to just use a one by four. Then, I made the repo. Most of it was writing the read me and just throwing in all the files and then also I went and found all the pieces that I needed and put it on the bill of materials.
